messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for customer NovusData in VPC 'vpc-novus-eu' using Dedicated Pool dp-novus-eu (eu-west-1). p99 = 2.3s (SLO 1.2s) · current window 5m. Auto-paging oncall.
lee (oncall-sre): on it. paging history shows same pool had 5% CPU rise ~2m ago. pulling logs now.
ana typo -> ana (sre): I've got traces from the proxy layer — tail latency looks correlated with KV cache miss rate. KV cache miss rate jumped from 6% -> 42% around 10:14 UTC.
jay (eng-runtime): putting context: this pool is on mixed-gen GPUs; we saw a small rolling maintenance earlier but nothing that should impact runtime. checking kernel metrics.
ravi (eng-ml): fwiw Novus is using model 'open-variant-xl' with long-context (1.8k). Memory pressure could cause KV eviction/prefetch thrash.
marta (acct-solutions): reaching out to Novus contact: @novus-admin — heads up we're investigating elevated p99s in your eu region. Do you see any traffic changes on your side?
novus-admin: we pushed a larger batch job at ~10:10 UTC that fans out many short-chat requests. noticing user complaints. please advise.
lee (oncall-sre): thanks. immediate plan: 1) isolate tenant traffic (rate-limit/burst) 2) enable fallback to quantized model 3) shift a portion of traffic to eu-central backup region. need ack from eng-runtime and ops-infra to run.
ops-infra: can do the routing shift and throttle. recommend partial shift (30-40%) to avoid cold-start spikes in eu-central.
jay (eng-runtime): suggest also enabling prefix KV hot-cache for Novus to reduce miss rate while we throttle. I can push a pool-level cache override.
ana -> ana (sre): running quick check: current pool CPU/gpu metrics:
```
gpu_util: 72% -> 85%
kv_cache_misses_1m: 6% -> 42%
request_qps: 220 -> 540 (for tenant novus)
avg_seq_len: 980 -> 1200
```
ana -> ana (sre): looks like tenant surge + longer sequences -> eviction.
ravi (eng-ml): fallback plan: switch Novus requests to 'open-variant-xl-quant' (4-bit quantized) — throughput increases ~1.8x and tail latency usually drops. small quality delta but should be acceptable short-term.
jay (eng-runtime): to enable fallback we need to register the model variant in routing policy and update customer's route config. I can do that; it takes ~30s to propagate.
lee (oncall-sre): marta, can you get Novus sign-off for temporary model fallback + partial regional failover? Need to confirm SLAs and customer impact messaging.
marta (acct-solutions): pinged Novus legal/ops: "we're going to route 35% traffic to eu-central and enable quantized fallback for remaining requests for up to 60 minutes unless you object". awaiting reply.
novus-admin: approved for 35% shift + fallback for 60 mins. please proceed.
ops-infra: executing throttle command to limit Novus bursty QPS and reduce noisy-neighbor impact. Running:
```
redwoodctl pools throttle --pool dp-novus-eu --tenant novus --max-qps 180
```
ops-infra: throttle applied. monitoring.
jay (eng-runtime): registering fallback route:
```
redwoodctl routes create --tenant novus --from model=open-variant-xl --to model=open-variant-xl-quant --percent 65 --priority fallback
```
jay (eng-runtime): fallback route created and propagated to edge nodes.
deploy-bot: route-update completed: route-id r-9c3f applied to 12 edge nodes.
ops-infra: initiating regional shift (35% of new requests) via smart-routing policy:
```
redwoodctl routing modify --tenant novus --policy weighted --weights eu-west-1=65,eu-central-1=35
```
ops-infra: shift in flight. starting warm-up of eu-central nodes to avoid cold latency.
ana -> ana (sre): after throttle + fallback + partial shift — re-checking metrics.
ana -> ana (sre): updating metrics snapshot:
```
p99: 2.3s -> 1.05s (target 1.2s)
kv_cache_miss: 42% -> 12%
request_qps: 540 -> 210 (novus)
```
ana -> ana (sre): phew — p99 back under SLO for the global mix. some requests routed to eu-central see +60-80ms extra network latency but overall p99 is healthy.
lee (oncall-sre): excellent. continuing to monitor for 30m. next steps: 1) keep fallback in place 2) analyze root cause for KV churn (hotspot detection) 3) capacity plan for dp-novus-eu or tenant isolation options.
jay (eng-runtime): will follow up with a config change to increase reserved KV hot-cache for Novus (temp). command queued:
```
redwoodctl cache override --pool dp-novus-eu --tenant novus --reserved-mb 2048 --duration 60m
```
ops-infra: override applied.
ravi (eng-ml): will run an eval comparing outputs prod vs quant fallback on a sampled set to quantify quality delta; report in 60m.
marta (acct-solutions): Novus ops confirmed they saw reduced errors and are fine with our actions. will send NRR to customer and prep a post-incident summary.
lee (oncall-sre): closing immediate paging. tagging for RCA: SRE, Eng Runtime, Eng ML, Infra. please create a follow-up ticket and link runbook.
novus-admin: thanks everyone for quick response. update me when RCA available.
deploy-bot: post-action note: routing rollback hooks set at 60m. no auto-rollback unless p99 > 1.2s for 10m.
lee (oncall-sre): logging incident timeline and actions to incident tracker. I'll hand off to the on-call rotation for next 4 hours for observation.
ana -> ana (sre): small note — ticket created: INC-2026 — assigned to lee + jay + ravi. initial notes in ticket.
marta (acct-solutions): I'll draft customer-facing timeline and impact statement. expected to be ready in 90m.
lee (oncall-sre): thanks all. stay on-call until 10:55 UTC if you're tagged. closing thread here but will append updates to the ticket. :white_check_mark:"
